# Three unit positives and one fractional positive: an exact endpoint theorem

For every integer m>=3 and p in[0,1], define

    P_m(p)=Pr(Gamma(3)+p Exp(1)
              >=Exp(1)+[(2+p)/m] Gamma(m)),

with all variables independent. Then

    P_m(p)>=min{P_m(0),P_m(1)}.                       (1)

The endpoints have saturated positive coefficients. This completes the k=3 fractional family for arbitrary m. Together with the k=1 and k=2 endpoint theorems and the proved exclusion p<=b, it covers all fractional minimizing patterns in ambient coefficient dimensions d<=9; the general-k endpoint theorem is not asserted here.

## 1. Actual density and derivative

Split the fractional-positive Exp and the Gamma(m) variable as T~Gamma(m+1) and an independent U~Beta(1,m). Put W=Gamma(3)-Exp(1), Z=W/T, and b=(2+p)/m. As in the independently verified k=2 proof,

    P_m'(p)=I(p)/(p+b)^(m+1),
    I(p)=integral_(-p)^b (p+z)^(m-1)
                          [2-(m+1)z] f_Z(z) dz.     (2)

The densities derived directly from W and T are

    f_Z(z)=(m+1)/[8(1-z)^(m+2)]                  (z<0),
    f_Z(z)=(m+1)/8 sum_(j=0)^2
        2^j binom(m+j+1,j) z^j/(1+z)^(m+j+2)     (z>=0).

The negative part of I is

    p^m[2(m+1)+(3m+1)p]/[8m(1+p)^2].

For the positive part set t=(p+z)/(1+z), whose endpoints are p and
T_*=N/(m+p+2), with N=(m+1)p+2. After dividing by t^(m-1), the transformed integrand is

    (m+1)/(8(1-p)^4) [2+(m+1)p-(m+3)t] S(t),

where

    S(t)=(1-p)^2+2(m+2)(1-p)(t-p)
                        +2(m+2)(m+3)(t-p)^2.

The verifier starts with the displayed actual f_Z and checks this substitution including its Jacobian. Thus it does not merely verify an internally stipulated polynomial.

Expand [2+(m+1)p-(m+3)t]S(t)=sum_(j=0)^3 C_jt^j and set
Q(t)=sum_(j=0)^3 C_jt^j/(m+j). Define

    A(p)=(2m^2+12m+17)p^4+(10m^2+52m+62)p^3
          +(9m^2+36m+45)p^2-(12m^2+36m+20)p
          +3m^2+8m+4,
    D(p)=p^2+(2m+4)p+m+4.

Exact simplification gives

    Q(T_*)=N^2 A(p)/[m(m+1)(m+p+2)^3],

and

    [2(m+1)+(3m+1)p]/[8m(1+p)^2]
       -(m+1)Q(p)/[8(1-p)^4]
      =-2p^3 D(p)/[m(1-p)^4(1+p)^2].

Therefore

    I(p)=N^(m+2) A(p)/[8m(1-p)^4(m+p+2)^(m+3)]
          -2p^(m+3) D(p)/[m(1-p)^4(1+p)^2].         (3)

All these identities are verified with m a free symbol.

## 2. Positivity of A

Write A=m^2 F+mG+H, where

    F=2p^4+10p^3+9p^2-12p+3,
    G=12p^4+52p^3+36p^2-36p+8,
    H=17p^4+62p^3+45p^2-20p+4.

All three are positive for p>=0. Indeed F''>=18, so the quadratic tangent lower bound at p=3/8 gives

    F(p)>=F(3/8)+F'(3/8)(p-3/8)+9(p-3/8)^2
          >=5279/16384>0,

using F(3/8)=681/2048 and F'(3/8)=-39/64. Likewise G''>=72, and the tangent quadratic at p=1/4 gives

    G(p)>=G(1/4)-G'(1/4)^2/144
          =135/64-25/64=55/32>0.

Finally H''>=90 and the tangent quadratic at zero gives

    H(p)>=4-20p+45p^2>=16/9>0.

The lower bounds on second derivatives hold everywhere on[0,infinity), so these tangent inequalities also hold on that full interval. Consequently A>0 for p>=0. D is plainly positive there.

## 3. A single turning point of the exact ratio

For p>0 define

    R(p)=16p^(m+3)(m+p+2)^(m+3)D(p)
              /[(1+p)^2 N^(m+2) A(p)].             (4)

For 0<p<1, (3) shows that I, and hence P_m', has the sign of 1-R. Logarithmic differentiation gives

    R'/R=(p-1)^3 K_m(p)
              /[p(1+p)(m+p+2) N D(p) A(p)],        (5)

where the coefficients of the sextic K, in ascending powers, are

    [p^0]K=-6m^5-70m^4-308m^3-632m^2-592m-192,
    [p^1]K=-15m^5-173m^4-762m^3-1588m^2-1512m-480,
    [p^2]K=3m^5-7m^4-260m^3-1006m^2-1308m-480,
    [p^3]K=34m^5+249m^4+594m^3+369m^2-298m-240,
    [p^4]K=22m^5+189m^4+558m^3+643m^2+180m-60,
    [p^5]K=4m^5+44m^4+164m^3+241m^2+111m-6,
    [p^6]K=2m^4+14m^3+29m^2+17m.

For m>=3 the coefficient signs are

    -, -, arbitrary, +, +, +, +.

For the only entries whose positivity is not immediate, it suffices even to use m>=1: the p^3 coefficient is at least708m^2, the p^4 coefficient is at least583m^2, and the p^5 coefficient is at least235m^2. Thus, omitting zeros, there is exactly one sign change. Descartes' rule, together with the negative constant coefficient and positive leading coefficient, proves that K has exactly one positive root c, with multiplicity one, and changes there from negative to positive.

On (0,1), the factor (p-1)^3 is negative. Hence R increases up to c and decreases thereafter, restricted to that interval. Its endpoint values are

    lim_(p down to0)R(p)=0,      R(1)=1.

If c>=1, R<1 throughout(0,1). If c<1, the strict decrease from c to1 gives R(c)>1, so R crosses1 exactly once on the increasing part and stays above1 afterward until reaching1 at the endpoint. Therefore 1-R, and hence P_m', changes sign at most once, only from positive to negative.

P_m is consequently increasing throughout, or first increasing and then decreasing. In either case its minimum on[0,1] is attained at an endpoint. Continuity there follows by coupling and the independent continuous term -Exp(1), which rules out boundary mass. This proves (1).

Every symbolic identity is checked in `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_three_unit_fractional_endpoint_symbolic.py`; the proof itself uses exact formulas and Descartes' rule for all m>=3.
